items.title: 日元重啟升勢衝破153關卡！日銀升息預期再起 華爾街對後市續強立場分歧
items.title_en: Yen Resumes Rise, Breaks Through 153 Barrier! BOJ Rate‑Hike Expectations Revive, Wall Street Remains Divided on Future Outlook
paras: 在市場對日本銀行(BOJ, 央行)加速升息的預期心理下，日元近日重啟升勢，一度升破153關卡，但這波漲勢能否延續下去，華爾街分析師看法依然分歧。
日元本月以來已上漲4%，成為市場焦點，也撼動了熱門的套利交易(carry trade)。在套利交易中，投資人以低廉成本借入日元，轉而投資收益率更高的其他貨幣及資產。
日元兌美元周三(9日)攀升至153.33日元，逼近周二觸及的七個月高點152.89日元。日元兌歐元、英鎊，以及墨西哥披索、土耳其里拉等熱門的套利交易標的也都呈現升值。
推動這波走勢的因素，包括市場預期日銀將加快緊縮腳步、日本投資人可能將海外資金匯回國內，以及華府要求日元升值的壓力。
交易員普遍預期日銀將在9月17-18日的會議上升息1碼(25個基點)，但日元能否延續漲勢，將取決於總裁植田和男後續是否展現鷹派態度。不過，最大的不確定因素仍將是美國聯準會(Fed)。
富國銀行(Wells Fargo)策略師Erik Nelson表示，日銀可能難以實現超出市場目前預期的更多升息，這將限制日元進一步升值空間。
摩根大通(JPMorgan Chase)全球外匯策略共同主管Meera Chandan則認為，日元走強這件事本身，可能降低日銀升息的誘因，「日本可能不希望日元比我們目前看到的水準弱太多，也不希望日元大幅走強。」
Chandan說：「因此，當日元接近150的低檔區間時，要進一步推升日元的門檻會更高，尤其是在Fed也採取鷹派立場的情況下。」
另一方面，美國銀行(BofA)策略師Alex Cohen早在6月就建議做多日元，如今則認為，若日銀如預期收緊貨幣政策，將為日元提供另一項上漲催化劑。
Cohen說：「如果日元維持在目前這些較低水準，日本出口商可能開始匯回海外資金，這可能成為日元新一波上漲的催化劑。」
宏利投信(Manulife Investment Management)多元資產解決方案團隊投資長(CIO)Nathan Thoof表示，只要日銀決策官員確認進一步緊縮政策仍在考慮之列，日元就會持續獲得支撐。
Thoof說：「現在壓力轉向日銀，央行必須證明市場預期有其依據，尤其要看今年底前是否會再升息一次。」
花旗(Citigroup)策略師Osamu Takashima、Daniel Tobon與Brian Levine說，日元走勢取決於Fed下周將採取的行動。「目前的動能可能將美元兌日元推向152左右。即便如此，如果Fed升息，要保持在155以下仍將相當困難。」
paras_en: Amid market expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will accelerate rate hikes, the yen has recently resumed its ascent, briefly breaking the 153 level, but analysts on Wall Street remain split on whether the rally can continue.

The yen has risen about 4% this month, becoming a market focus and shaking up popular carry‑trade strategies, where investors borrow yen at low cost to invest in higher‑yielding currencies and assets.

On Wednesday the 9th, the yen climbed to ¥153.33 per dollar, nearing the seven‑month high of ¥152.89 hit on Tuesday, while the yen’s value versus the euro, pound, Mexican peso and Turkish lira – other common carry‑trade targets – also appreciated.

Drivers of the move include expectations that the BOJ will tighten policy faster, the possibility that Japanese investors will repatriate overseas funds, and pressure from Washington for a stronger yen.

Traders broadly expect the BOJ to raise rates by one step (25 basis points) at its September 17‑18 meeting, but whether the yen can keep rising will depend on whether Governor Kazuo Ueda shows a hawkish stance thereafter. The biggest uncertainty, however, remains the U.S. Federal Reserve.
Wells Fargo strategist Erik Nelson said the BOJ is unlikely to deliver rate hikes beyond what the market already anticipates, which will cap further yen appreciation.

JPMorgan Chase global FX strategy co‑head Meera Chandan argued that a stronger yen itself may reduce the incentive for BOJ hikes, noting Japan may not want the yen to be much weaker than current levels nor see it surge dramatically.
Chandan added that when the yen is near the low‑150 range, pushing it higher becomes more difficult, especially if the Fed also adopts a hawkish stance.
Conversely, Bank of America strategist Alex Cohen, who advocated buying yen back in June, now believes that if the BOJ tightens as expected, it will provide another catalyst for yen gains.
Cohen said that if the yen stays at these relatively low levels, Japanese exporters may start bringing overseas funds back home, which could spark a new wave of yen appreciation.
Manulife Investment Management’s multi‑asset solutions CIO Nathan Thoof said that as long as BOJ policymakers keep further tightening on the table, the yen will continue to receive support.
Thoof noted that pressure is now shifting to the BOJ, which must prove market expectations are justified, especially whether another rate hike will occur before year‑end.

Citigroup strategists Osamu Takashima, Daniel Tobon and Brian Levine said the yen’s path depends on the Fed’s actions next week, adding that current momentum could push USD/JPY toward the 152 area, but keeping it below 155 would be tough if the Fed raises rates.

items.title: 34年前「金融偷獵者」 大獲全勝 貝森特改換角色當莊家
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)本周展現出極具戰術性的貨幣政策風格，公開向外匯交易員喊話，大膽宣告「我現在就是莊家」。他強調自己對日本央行與日本政策制定者的行動擁有「資訊不對稱」優勢，並直接挑戰市場交易員敢不敢與他作對。
這種將主導權掌握在手的強硬作風，深深植根於他34年前協助索羅斯「擊潰英格蘭銀行」的頂尖避險基金經歷。
據《Fortune》記者Eva Roytburg報導，1992年時年僅29歲的貝森特洞察到英格蘭銀行的致命弱點：央行承諾將英鎊維持在歐洲匯率機制(ERM)的狹幅區間內，但透過升息來保衛匯率的做法，會嚴重打擊當時持有浮動利率房貸的英國屋主。
貝森特成功說服老闆索羅斯對英鎊發動大規模做空，最終迫使英國退出ERM，並為基金賺進10億美元利潤。Roytburg總結，貝森特從中汲取的關鍵教訓是：「當央行人為將貨幣維持在市場無法支持的水準時，市場最終將會獲勝」。
34年後，貝森特角色互換，從昔日的「金融偷獵者」變成了坐鎮局面的「金融護林員」。據報導，貝森特目前正與日本當局協調購買日元，且他多次暗示希望東京當局調升利率，而非僅依賴反覆干預。在他的警告與干預下，美元兌日元匯率已從2026年7月的163上方，一路回落至9月8日的153.96。
然而，這套強硬手法也在內部引發質疑；昔日索羅斯時期的同僚Stanley Druckenmiller公開指責他介入債券市場是個錯誤，而貝森特則反駁稱，擴大買回舊美債旨在冷卻美國公債市場的「發燒」現象。
據《路透》報導，日本央行預計在即將召開的會議上提高基準利率，這成為驗證貝森特威懾是否有效的即時測試。若日本當局順利升息，貝森特的豪賭就能成立；若日本猶豫不決，這位曾寫下狙擊央行教科書的掌權者，將親自驗證市場規律是否會反噬自己。

items.title: G10貨幣黑馬恐失色！主要央行升息潮壓頂 英鎊漲勢面臨回檔危機
items.title_en: G10 Currency Dark Horse May Lose Its Luster! Central Bank Rate‑Hike Wave Peaks, Pound’s Rise Faces Pull‑Back Risk
paras: 儘管英國政府再次更迭、地緣政治帶來衝擊，英鎊大致上未受影響，今年來表現優於許多主要貨幣，然而，近期這股動能逐漸減弱，而且疲弱走勢恐怕將進一步加劇。
今年以來，英鎊兌歐元升值約1.6%，兌瑞士法郎升值2.8%，兌瑞典克朗升值4.9%，兌加拿大元升值1%。同期間，英鎊兌美元大致持平，兌日元則貶值1.3%。
英國前首相施凱爾(Keir Starmer)7月20日辭職後，英國迎接10年內第七位上台的領導人，市場密切關注新政府是否會遵守前財政大臣Rachel Reeves強調的「財政規則」。
在同樣來自中間偏左工黨的資深政治人物柏南(Andy Burnham)上台後，英國長期借貸成本走高，但這與全球政府公債遭拋售的走勢同步。

英國長期借貸成本創1998年以來最高

金融服務公司Ebury市場策略主管Matthew Ryan表示，過去三個月以來，英鎊是G10富裕國家貨幣中「意外強勢的貨幣」，主要歸因於英國經濟韌性超乎預期。
英國第2季國內生產毛額(GDP)成長0.4%，第1季則成長0.6%，在已開發經濟體中表現數一數二強勁。晴朗天氣以及FIFA世界盃帶來的熱潮提振消費支出，而儘管地緣政治局勢動盪，企業活動仍展現超乎預期的韌性。
Rabobank資深外匯策略師Jane Foley表示，4月伊朗衝突爆發初期，，由於市場預期英國央行(BOE)將為因應通膨疑慮而升息，成為當時支撐英鎊的力量。
英國易受油價及天然氣價格上漲的影響，而這兩種天然資源今年均大幅上漲，導致整體通膨率升抵近3%水準。

英鎊弱勢可能加劇？

儘管物價壓力再度升溫，英國央行迄今仍將基準利率維持在3.75%。
目前市場定價顯示，英國9月17日會議升息的機率偏低。相較之下，市場高度預期歐洲央行(ECB)本周將升息，對聯準會(Fed)本月17日升息的預期也日益升高。
Rabobank的Foley指出，在柏南政府10月28日將公布首份年度預算案，市場正為此感到不安之際，英國央行下周若釋出鴿派訊息，將「進一步讓英鎊暴露在風險之中」。
英國新任財政大臣John Healey周一在演講中表示，他仍將致力於維持財政紀律，同時希望讓經濟成長更平均分布於英國各地，而非集中在經濟核心倫敦。
摩根大通英國經濟學家Allan Monks表示，他的談話顯示，在借貸成本上揚的背景下，政府對稅收及支出政策的調整將採取審慎態度。預算案可能繼續聚焦於地方分權、提高公共服務的政府控制，以及與民間部門建立更多合作關係，但對整體經濟展望的改變有限。
Ebury的Ryan表示，這份預算案具有高度政治風險，可能包含「提高附加稅率以及增加發債」，以支應柏南政府的支出計畫。
他表示，相關措施可能包括調整房產購買稅及地方政府稅、引進「豪宅稅」，以及收緊退休金與個人投資帳戶的稅務優惠。他補充，若市場認為相關措施可能抑制經濟成長並壓縮民間部門，同時又需要增加借款，市場將對此感到不安。
paras_en: Despite a reshuffled UK government and geopolitical shocks, the pound has largely been unaffected and has outperformed many major currencies this year, but its momentum has recently been waning and a weak trend could worsen further.

Since the start of the year the pound has appreciated about 1.6% against the euro, 2.8% against the Swiss franc, 4.9% against the Swedish krona and 1% against the Canadian dollar. Over the same period it has been roughly flat versus the US dollar and down 1.3% versus the Japanese yen.

After former Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigned on July 20, the UK welcomed its seventh leader in ten years, and markets are watching closely whether the new administration will adhere to the “fiscal rules” emphasized by former finance minister Rachel Reeves.
Following the ascent of senior Labour figure Andy Burnham, long‑term borrowing costs in the UK have risen, a trend that mirrors the global sell‑off of sovereign bonds.

Long‑term borrowing costs in the UK have hit their highest level since 1998. Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at financial‑services firm Ebury, said the pound has been the “surprisingly strong currency” among G10 affluent‑nation currencies over the past three months, mainly because the UK economy’s resilience has exceeded expectations.

UK GDP grew 0.4% in Q2 after a 0.6% gain in Q1, making it one of the strongest performers among developed economies. Sunny weather and the FIFA World Cup hype boosted consumer spending, and despite geopolitical turbulence, business activity showed unexpectedly robust resilience.

Rabobank senior FX strategist Jane Foley noted that when the Iran conflict erupted in early April, markets expected the Bank of England to raise rates to combat inflation, which at the time supported the pound.
The UK is vulnerable to rising oil and natural‑gas prices, both of which have surged sharply this year, pushing overall inflation close to the 3% level.
Could a weaker pound exacerbate the situation? Although price pressures have heated up again, the Bank of England has kept its policy rate at 3.75% so far.

Current market pricing shows a low probability of a rate hike at the BoE meeting on September 17. By contrast, markets heavily anticipate an ECB hike this week and are increasingly pricing in a Fed hike on the 17th of this month.

Foley of Rabobank warned that with Burnham’s government set to unveil its first annual budget on October 28 and markets already uneasy, a dovish signal from the BoE next week would “further expose the pound to risk”.

New finance minister John Healey told a speech on Monday that he will continue to uphold fiscal discipline while aiming to spread economic growth more evenly across the UK rather than concentrating it in the core economy of London.

Morgan Stanley economist Allan Monks said his comments indicate that, against a backdrop of rising borrowing costs, the government will take a cautious approach to tax and spending policy adjustments. The budget is likely to keep focusing on devolution, tighter public‑service oversight and more public‑private partnerships, with limited impact on the overall economic outlook.
Ryan of Ebury said the budget carries high political risk and may include “higher surcharge rates and increased borrowing” to fund Burnham’s spending plans.

He added that measures could involve changes to property purchase tax and local‑government tax, the introduction of a “luxury‑home tax”, and tighter tax breaks for pensions and individual investment accounts, and warned that if markets think such steps could curb growth, squeeze the private sector and require more borrowing, anxiety would rise.

items.title: 日元急升散戶逆勢加碼看空 淨空頭部位達3.61兆日元
items.title_en: Yen Soars Rapidly as Retail Traders Double Down on Short Bets, Net Short Position Hits ¥3.61 trillion
paras: 日元兌美元匯率近期急劇反彈至數月來高點，但日本散戶並未改變對日元的看空立場，反而維持傳統「逆勢操作」習慣，持續加碼日元淨空頭倉位。
根據日本金融期貨協會及東京金融交易所資料，上周日本散戶持有的日元淨空頭部位，估計達約 3.61 兆日元(約 235 億美元)，高於 8 月水準；此前 7 月的日元空頭部位更一度衝上 4.41 兆日元，創下自 2015 年以來最高紀錄。
本月以來，日元兌美元已升值約 4%，一度突破 153 關卡並觸及 152 日元水位。推動這波升勢的主因包括市場預期日本央行將進一步升息，以及外界揣測日本政府退休金投資基金(GPIF)等機構，可能調整資產配置，帶動日元強勁需求並觸發大規模停損賣單。
這與海外投資者的行為形成鮮明對比——外資急於解除日元套利交易，部分避險基金甚至押注美元兌日元在年底前將跌破 150 關卡。
瑞穗銀行高級策略師中島將行警告，若日元持續走強，散戶最終恐被迫平倉美元多頭，停損引發的美元拋售可能進一步推升日元。
SBI Liquidity Market 常務董事鈴木亮補充，美元跌破 155 後散戶追買美元的傾向已略微放緩，且散戶自發停損意願有所提高，但若匯率持續單邊升值，部分高槓桿部位仍面臨強制平倉的風險。
paras_en: The yen‑dollar exchange rate has surged sharply to a multi‑month high, yet Japanese retail investors have not altered their bearish stance on the yen; instead, they continue their traditional contrarian habit by adding to their net short yen positions.

According to data from the Japan Financial Futures Association and the Tokyo Financial Exchange, last week Japanese retail investors held net short yen positions estimated at about ¥3.61 trillion (roughly $23.5 billion), higher than the August level; earlier, the July short position had briefly spiked to ¥4.41 trillion, the highest since 2015.

Since the start of the month the yen has appreciated about 4% against the dollar, briefly breaking the 153‑yen barrier and touching the 152‑yen level. The rally is driven mainly by market expectations that the Bank of Japan will raise rates further and speculation that institutional investors such as the Government Pension Investment Fund may rebalance assets, sparking strong yen demand and triggering large stop‑loss sell orders.

This contrasts sharply with overseas investors’ behavior—foreign capital is rushing to unwind yen‑carry trades, and some hedge funds are even betting that the dollar‑yen pair will fall below the 150 level before year‑end.

Mizuho Bank senior strategist Nakashima warned that if the yen keeps strengthening, retail traders may eventually be forced to close their long‑dollar positions, and the resulting dollar sell‑off could push the yen even higher.

SBI Liquidity Market executive director Suzuki Ryo added that after the dollar slipped below 155, retail appetite for buying dollars has eased slightly and their willingness to stop‑loss has risen, but if the exchange rate continues its one‑sided appreciation, some highly leveraged positions still face the risk of forced liquidation.

items.title: 美元走勢疲軟逼近7個月低點 美債回購與通膨數據成焦點
items.title_en: Dollar Weakness Near 7-Month Low as Treasury Buybacks and Inflation Data Take Center Stage
paras: 隨著日元強勁反彈以及市場緊盯美國財政部即將公布的公債回購計畫與通膨數據，美元指數已逼近近7個月來的最低點。
彭博美元指數周三(9日)一度下跌0.2%，創下自2月18日以來的最低。其中，日元作為指數的第二大組成貨幣，當天上升0.5%，將本月的累計漲幅擴大至約4%。
美元走勢承壓，部分源於美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)的強硬表態。貝森特公開向交易員發起挑戰，要求市場試探他壓低美債殖利率與強化日元的決心，並準備透過擴大公債回購計畫來抑制殖利率。美財政部預計於周三稍晚宣布買回10年期至20年期在外流通公債的具體規模。
傑富瑞(Jefferies)歐洲首席經濟學家兼策略師Mohit Kumar表示，買回規模需超過40億美元才能對市場產生實質影響，首波操作規模不排除達到80億至100億美元；不過摩根大通研究人員則認為財政部可能不會透露更多細節。
另一方面，市場正密切關注周五公布的美國通膨數據，此數據將塑造聯準會(Fed)下周的政策決策方向，目前貨幣市場預估升息一碼(0.25個百分點)的機率約為60%。
整體而言，期權指標顯示交易員短期內對美元維持看空態度。然而，受美伊交火影響，布蘭特原油已上漲至每桶100美元，高企的能源價格對歐元與英鎊構成壓力，使美元對這兩大貨幣仍有進一步走高的空間。
paras_en: As the yen rebounds strongly and markets focus on the U.S. Treasury’s upcoming bond buyback plan and inflation data, the dollar index has edged close to its lowest level in nearly seven months.

The Bloomberg dollar index fell 0.2% on Wednesday the 9th, hitting its lowest point since February 18. The yen, the index’s second‑largest component, rose 0.5% that day, expanding its month‑to‑date gain to about 4%.

The dollar’s pressure stems in part from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s hard‑line stance. Bessent publicly challenged traders to test his resolve to push down Treasury yields and strengthen the yen, and said the Treasury is ready to expand its bond‑buyback program to curb yields. The Treasury plans to announce later Wednesday the specific size of the buyback of outstanding 10‑ to 20‑year bonds.

Jefferies Europe chief economist and strategist Mohit Kumar said the buyback would need to exceed $4 billion to have a material market impact, with the first tranche possibly reaching $8‑10 billion; however, JPMorgan researchers think the Treasury may not disclose further details.

Meanwhile, markets are closely watching U.S. inflation data due on Friday, which will shape the Fed’s policy direction next week. Money‑market participants currently estimate about a 60% probability of a 0.25‑percentage‑point rate hike.

Overall, options indicators show traders remain short on the dollar in the short term. Yet, amid the Israel‑Iran clash, Brent crude has risen to $100 a barrel, and the high energy prices are pressuring the euro and pound, leaving room for the dollar to climb further against those two major currencies.

items.title: 日元重啟升勢衝破153關卡！日銀升息預期再起 華爾街對後市續強立場分歧
items.title_en: Yen Resumes Rise, Breaks Through 153 Barrier! BOJ Rate‑Hike Expectations Revive, Wall Street Remains Divided on Future Outlook
paras: 在市場對日本銀行(BOJ, 央行)加速升息的預期心理下，日元近日重啟升勢，一度升破153關卡，但這波漲勢能否延續下去，華爾街分析師看法依然分歧。
日元本月以來已上漲4%，成為市場焦點，也撼動了熱門的套利交易(carry trade)。在套利交易中，投資人以低廉成本借入日元，轉而投資收益率更高的其他貨幣及資產。
日元兌美元周三(9日)攀升至153.33日元，逼近周二觸及的七個月高點152.89日元。日元兌歐元、英鎊，以及墨西哥披索、土耳其里拉等熱門的套利交易標的也都呈現升值。
推動這波走勢的因素，包括市場預期日銀將加快緊縮腳步、日本投資人可能將海外資金匯回國內，以及華府要求日元升值的壓力。
交易員普遍預期日銀將在9月17-18日的會議上升息1碼(25個基點)，但日元能否延續漲勢，將取決於總裁植田和男後續是否展現鷹派態度。不過，最大的不確定因素仍將是美國聯準會(Fed)。
富國銀行(Wells Fargo)策略師Erik Nelson表示，日銀可能難以實現超出市場目前預期的更多升息，這將限制日元進一步升值空間。
摩根大通(JPMorgan Chase)全球外匯策略共同主管Meera Chandan則認為，日元走強這件事本身，可能降低日銀升息的誘因，「日本可能不希望日元比我們目前看到的水準弱太多，也不希望日元大幅走強。」
Chandan說：「因此，當日元接近150的低檔區間時，要進一步推升日元的門檻會更高，尤其是在Fed也採取鷹派立場的情況下。」
另一方面，美國銀行(BofA)策略師Alex Cohen早在6月就建議做多日元，如今則認為，若日銀如預期收緊貨幣政策，將為日元提供另一項上漲催化劑。
Cohen說：「如果日元維持在目前這些較低水準，日本出口商可能開始匯回海外資金，這可能成為日元新一波上漲的催化劑。」
宏利投信(Manulife Investment Management)多元資產解決方案團隊投資長(CIO)Nathan Thoof表示，只要日銀決策官員確認進一步緊縮政策仍在考慮之列，日元就會持續獲得支撐。
Thoof說：「現在壓力轉向日銀，央行必須證明市場預期有其依據，尤其要看今年底前是否會再升息一次。」
花旗(Citigroup)策略師Osamu Takashima、Daniel Tobon與Brian Levine說，日元走勢取決於Fed下周將採取的行動。「目前的動能可能將美元兌日元推向152左右。即便如此，如果Fed升息，要保持在155以下仍將相當困難。」
paras_en: Amid market expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will accelerate rate hikes, the yen has recently resumed its ascent, briefly breaking the 153 level, but analysts on Wall Street remain split on whether the rally can continue.

The yen has risen about 4% this month, becoming a market focus and shaking up popular carry‑trade strategies, where investors borrow yen at low cost to invest in higher‑yielding currencies and assets.

On Wednesday the 9th, the yen climbed to ¥153.33 per dollar, nearing the seven‑month high of ¥152.89 hit on Tuesday, while the yen’s value versus the euro, pound, Mexican peso and Turkish lira – other common carry‑trade targets – also appreciated.

Drivers of the move include expectations that the BOJ will tighten policy faster, the possibility that Japanese investors will repatriate overseas funds, and pressure from Washington for a stronger yen.

Traders broadly expect the BOJ to raise rates by one step (25 basis points) at its September 17‑18 meeting, but whether the yen can keep rising will depend on whether Governor Kazuo Ueda shows a hawkish stance thereafter. The biggest uncertainty, however, remains the U.S. Federal Reserve.
Wells Fargo strategist Erik Nelson said the BOJ is unlikely to deliver rate hikes beyond what the market already anticipates, which will cap further yen appreciation.

JPMorgan Chase global FX strategy co‑head Meera Chandan argued that a stronger yen itself may reduce the incentive for BOJ hikes, noting Japan may not want the yen to be much weaker than current levels nor see it surge dramatically.
Chandan added that when the yen is near the low‑150 range, pushing it higher becomes more difficult, especially if the Fed also adopts a hawkish stance.
Conversely, Bank of America strategist Alex Cohen, who advocated buying yen back in June, now believes that if the BOJ tightens as expected, it will provide another catalyst for yen gains.
Cohen said that if the yen stays at these relatively low levels, Japanese exporters may start bringing overseas funds back home, which could spark a new wave of yen appreciation.
Manulife Investment Management’s multi‑asset solutions CIO Nathan Thoof said that as long as BOJ policymakers keep further tightening on the table, the yen will continue to receive support.
Thoof noted that pressure is now shifting to the BOJ, which must prove market expectations are justified, especially whether another rate hike will occur before year‑end.

Citigroup strategists Osamu Takashima, Daniel Tobon and Brian Levine said the yen’s path depends on the Fed’s actions next week, adding that current momentum could push USD/JPY toward the 152 area, but keeping it below 155 would be tough if the Fed raises rates.

items.title: 〈台幣〉匯市觀望氣氛轉濃 量縮升值3分收31.505元
items.title_en: TWD Forex Market Turns More Cautious as Volume Shrinks; Gains 0.03 to Close at 31.505
paras: 新台幣今(9)日全日維持升值走勢，不受美國聯準會9月升息機率過5成的干擾，終場收在31.505元，升值3分，台北外匯經紀公司成交值則縮至14.57億美元，顯示市場觀望氣氛轉趨濃厚。
新台幣今日以31.51元、升值2.5分開出後，最高來到31.455元，全日高低價差7.5分，呈現偏強整理。
觀察主要亞幣，日元和韓元續彈升超過0.2%，新台幣收升0.1%，人民幣和星元微幅升值，泰銖則微貶不到0.05%，美元指數小跌0.05%左右。
國泰證期研究部指出，只要油價未加速逼近 120美元、美債殖利率未失控且美股費半指數守穩，不致引發全面性翻空。
統一投顧則提到，市場靜待本周美國公布通膨數據以判讀下周FOMC利率決策路徑，回歸台股，目前技術面均線維持多頭排列，受惠新台幣升值熱錢買盤、AI 族群 8 月營收亮眼以及今晚蘋果新品發表會等利多題材，使台股低檔買盤具支撐。
paras_en: The New Taiwan dollar stayed on an appreciating trend throughout the day on the 9th, undisturbed by the Federal Reserve's over‑50% probability of a September rate hike, and closed at 31.505, up 0.03. Turnover at Taipei foreign‑exchange brokerages fell to $1.457 billion, indicating a growing wait‑and‑see mood in the market.
The TWD opened at 31.51, up 0.025, then rose to a high of 31.455; the intraday range was 0.075, showing a relatively strong consolidation.

Among the major Asian currencies, the yen and won each rose more than 0.2%, the New Taiwan dollar gained 0.1%, the renminbi and Singapore dollar edged higher, the Thai baht slipped slightly by less than 0.05%, and the U.S. dollar index fell about 0.05%.

Cathay Securities Research noted that as long as oil prices do not accelerate toward $120, U.S. Treasury yields remain under control and the S&P 500 half‑year index stays stable, a broad‑scale short‑covering is unlikely.

Unified Investment Advisory said the market is waiting for this week’s U.S. inflation data to gauge next week’s FOMC rate‑decision path. Regarding the Taiwan stock market, technical moving averages remain in a bullish arrangement; buoyed by the TWD’s appreciation attracting hot‑money buying, strong August earnings from AI stocks and tonight’s Apple product launch, the lower‑level buying support for the Taiwan index is solid.

items.title: 貝森特再挺日元的真實意圖是穩美債？ 專家：真正的黑天鵝是日債殖利率
items.title_en: Biden's Repeated Support for the Yen Is Really About Stabilizing U.S. Treasuries? Experts Say the Real Black Swan Is Japanese Bond Yields
paras: 美國財長貝森特周二(8日)在一場公開活動中再度口頭干預日元，市場已精準看出其背後意圖是想穩定美債市場，但分析人士提醒，日本國債殖利率近期飆升，或許才是美債面臨的真正風險。
貝森特向日元空頭直言，他正力推日元升值，憑藉身份握有「內幕優勢」。
貝森特說：「每當有人說財政部長是在冒險，我只想說這正是我夢寐以求的局面，我掌握着資訊不對稱的優勢。我現在就是莊家，干預日元時，我對日本央行及政策制定者的行動有深入了解。想和我對賭，大可放馬過來。」
他並回顧7月31日美日罕見聯合買入日元一事。對美國而言，疲軟日元會削弱關稅政策帶來的貿易優勢，引發的日債拋售潮還可能波及美債殖利率，這些正是美國協同干預的關鍵原因。
在7月底的干預行動中，美國財政部拋售儲備歐元、以所得資金買入日元，但幾天後日元升幅收窄，因市場認為美國買匯火力有限，且美日利差未縮小，美國罕見賣歐元而非美債籌資，亦引發猜測。
近來，在猜測日本將於本月假期交易清淡期間再度干預，以及市場押注日本央行(BOJ)升息的雙重因素下，日元自上週以來突然大漲。美元兌日元周二(8日)一度貶破153，最低觸及152.87，創7個月最低；自逼近164的40年低點以來，日元累計升值約7%。
摩根士丹利策略主管James Lord表示，市場對本月BOJ升息機率的押注飆升至98%，加上155關口失守觸發的止損盤，放大了日元漲勢。
與此同時，投資人擔憂上兆美元規模的日元套利交易再現平倉，但Lord認為，光靠日元走強不足以撼動新興市場套利交易，美日政策利率分別為3.50%~3.75%與約1%，利差優勢仍在且融資貨幣已擴大至歐元與瑞郎，單一貨幣影響減弱。
更值得警惕的是，隨著日本國債執利率攀升至近30年高點，日本龐大海外資金會否回流本土的長期風險正重新累積。儘管尚未出現大規模撤離跡象，已有機構警告市場低估了回流的可能性與速度。
多年的超低利率迫使日本投資者赴海外尋求收益，日本投資者持有海外資產近5兆美元，且是美債最大海外持有國，持有部位約1.1萬億美元。
但近期財政支出前景、通膨壓力及升息預期升溫，推動日債殖利率持續走高，10年期殖利率上周觸及3%，為1996年來首見。日本政府退休投資基金(GPIF)會否提高國內債券配置成為焦點，厚生勞動大臣上野賢一郎周二表示，GPIF仍在研究是否重新審視資產配置。
Vanguard國際利率主管Ales Koutny指出，若日本國債殖利率續升，更多資本可能回流，不僅關乎日元與日債，也可能影響美債、歐債及全球融資環境。
Marlborough基金經理James Athey更表示，回流條件已基本具備，因殖利率攀高、升息預期增強、利差縮小加上日元升值，日本投資人重新配置資產的動力正不斷增強。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen on Tuesday (the 8th) again verbally intervened in the yen at a public event, and the market has accurately inferred that her underlying motive is to stabilize the U.S. Treasury market, but analysts warn that the recent surge in Japanese government bond yields may actually be the true risk facing U.S. Treasuries.
Yellen told yen short sellers that she is actively pushing for yen appreciation, claiming she has an "insider advantage" because of her position.

Yellen said, "Whenever someone says the Treasury Secretary is taking a risk, I just want to say that's exactly the scenario I've been hoping for. I have the advantage of asymmetric information. I am the house now, and when I intervene in the yen I have deep insight into the actions of the Bank of Japan and policymakers. If you want to bet against me, bring it on."

She also recalled the rare joint U.S.-Japan purchase of yen on July 31. For the United States, a weak yen would erode the trade advantage provided by tariff policy, and the ensuing sell‑off in Japanese bonds could spill over into U.S. Treasury yields – the very reasons for coordinated U.S. intervention.

In the late‑July intervention, the U.S. Treasury sold its euro reserves and used the proceeds to buy yen, but the yen’s gains narrowed a few days later as markets judged that the U.S. buying power was limited, the U.S.–Japan rate spread had not narrowed, and the unusual sale of euros rather than U.S. Treasuries to raise funds sparked speculation.

Recently, amid speculation that Japan might intervene again during the thin‑trading holiday period this month and market bets on a Bank of Japan rate hike, the yen surged sharply since last week. The dollar/yen fell below 153 on Tuesday (the 8th), touching a low of 152.87 – a seven‑month low – and has appreciated about 7% since approaching the 40‑year low near 164.
Morgan Stanley strategy head James Lord said market odds of a BOJ rate hike this month have jumped to 98%, and stop‑loss orders triggered by the breach of the 155 level have amplified the yen’s rise.

At the same time, investors worry that a multi‑trillion‑dollar yen‑carry trade could unwind, but Lord believes that yen strength alone is insufficient to shake emerging‑market carry trades; the policy rate gap – 3.50%‑3.75% in the U.S. versus roughly 1% in Japan – still favors the carry, and financing currencies have expanded to the euro and Swiss franc, reducing the impact of any single currency.

More concerning is that as Japanese government bond yields climb toward a near‑30‑year high, the risk that Japan’s massive overseas capital will flow back home is re‑accumulating. Although no large‑scale outflows have yet materialized, some institutions warn that the market is underestimating the likelihood and speed of such repatriation.

Decades of ultra‑low rates have forced Japanese investors abroad in search of yield; Japanese investors now hold nearly $5 trillion in overseas assets and are the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, with a position of about $1.1 trillion.

But recent fiscal‑spending outlooks, inflation pressures and rising rate‑hike expectations have pushed Japanese bond yields higher, with the 10‑year yield hitting 3% last week – the first time since 1996. Whether the Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) will increase its domestic‑bond allocation is now a focus, and Labour Minister Kenichiro Ueno said on Tuesday that GPIF is still studying a possible reassessment of its asset mix.

Vanguard’s international rates chief Ales Koutny noted that if Japanese bond yields keep rising, more capital could flow back to Japan, affecting not only the yen and JGBs but also U.S. Treasuries, European bonds and the global financing environment.

Marlborough fund manager James Athey added that the conditions for repatriation are essentially in place: higher yields, stronger rate‑hike expectations, narrowing spreads and a stronger yen are all boosting Japanese investors’ incentive to re‑allocate assets back home.

items.title: 日元本月狂升4%、美元逼近7個月低點 市場緊盯美債回購規模
paras: 隨著日元(USDJPY) 走強，美元逼近近7個月低點，交易員正等待美國財政部本周稍晚公布債券回購計畫及通膨數據。
彭博美元即期指數周三(9日)一度下跌0.2%，逼近2月18日以來最低水準。美元(DXY) 走弱主要受到日元上漲拖累，日元是該指數權重第二大的貨幣。日元周三升值0.5%，本月迄今漲幅擴大至約4%。
美國財政部長貝森特向交易員喊話，儘管考驗他推升日元的決心，並表示自己如今對市場走勢作出判斷時，實際上等同掌握內部資訊。
這番言論是貝森特試圖引導市場走勢以來，措辭最強硬的表態之一，也讓美元再度承壓。
貝森特也將公布擴大債券回購計畫的初步規模，顯示他願意採取多大力度來壓低美債殖利率。美國財政部預計周三稍晚宣布，隔日回購流通在外10年至20年期公債的操作規模。
Jefferies International歐洲首席經濟學家暨策略師Mohit Kumar表示：「若要對市場產生影響，貝森特首次回購規模必須超過40億美元；即使首次操作規模大得多，可能達到80億至100億美元，我們也不會感到意外。」
不過，摩根大通研究人員認為，美國財政部可能不會進一步透露債券回購操作的規模。
交易員也聚焦本周五(11日)公布的美國通膨數據，該數據可能影響市場對聯準會（Fed）下周政策決策的預期。貨幣市場目前預估，Fed升息1碼的機率約為60%。
選擇權指標顯示，整體而言，交易員短期內仍看空美元。不過，由於能源價格居高不下，對歐元與英鎊構成格外沉重的壓力，市場仍認為美元兌這兩種貨幣有進一步升值空間。
